title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
technique: reuse precomputed non-prefix KV caches and selectively recompute a small subset of high-deviation tokens, pipelined with KV loading

optimized_metrics.evidence: CacheBlend reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 2.2-3.3x and increases the inference throughput by 2.8-5x from full KV recompute without compromising generation quality
increases the inference throughput by 2.8-5x from full KV recompute
how to quickly combine their precomputed KV caches in order to achieve the same generation quality as the expensive full prefill

headline_claim.text: CacheBlend reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 2.2-3.3x and increases the inference throughput by 2.8-5x from full KV recompute without compromising generation quality.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Thus, the prefill delay determines the time to first token (TTFT).
metric_definitions.notes: prefill-delay based; the paper uses an 'extra delay on TTFT' notion for loading/recompute pipelining; queueing appears in Fig 14 via request rate

metric_definitions.definition_quote: It measures the similarity between the model's output and the ground-truth answer of the question based on the number of overlapping words.
demonstrates that prefill can be a throughput bottleneck, by the IT department
metric_definitions.notes: throughput unit not formally defined; plotted as average request rate per second vs TTFT (Fig 14)

load_regime: request-rate sweep (Poisson-style average request rate vs TTFT, Fig 14); also batch size / chunk number sweeps
tradeoff_acknowledged: slightly lower quality (<=0.015 F1 loss) vs full recompute; slower than full KV reuse in TTFT
hardware: RunPod 2x NVIDIA A40, 128GB RAM, NVMe SSD 4.8 GB/s
extractor_notes: Throughput is stated in abstract but never formally defined; it is shown as sustainable request rate at a TTFT level.
